rawItems.title: Man accused of sexually assaulting woman near primary school named
rawItems.content:
A man accused of sexually assaulting a woman near a Huntingdonshire primary school has been named by police. Officers were called at around 7.25am on May 26 with reports of a sexual assault on a woman in her 50s in Ramsey Road, St Ives. He also faces two counts of using threatening/abusive words/behaviour likely to cause harassment, alarm or distress. He is due to appear at Cambridge Magistrates’ Court on November 5. rawItems.title: Reform councillor arrested over alleged false statements in election papers
rawItems.content: A Reform UK council group leader in Cambridgeshire has been arrested on suspicion of making false statements in election nomination papers. Representing the Ramsey Ward, Ryan Coogan was elected to Huntingdonshire District Council in the local elections on May 7. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed a man was arrested on September 24 on suspicion of making false statements in nomination papers. The 42-year-old from Waterbeach has since been released on bail to return to Milton Police Station on December 22. Coogan told The Hunts Post he has "worked and will continue to work with the police as part of the investigation". It comes after the force revealed it had launched an investigation into the alleged false statements shortly after the May election. A spokesperson said the inquiry relates to Coogan and the most recent election, though it has not disclosed the nature of the alleged statements. At the time, a spokesperson for Huntingdonshire District Council said: "We are aware of a police referral in relation to the recent district council elections. "As this matter is a live investigation, it would not be appropriate for the council or the returning officer to comment further at this stage." Coogan previously ran as Reform UK's candidate in the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough mayoral election, coming second last year.
